minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 5, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 5:03
p.m., on Monday, January 5, 2009, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on December 23, 2008, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

ROLL CALL

Present:  Council Member Kelley (arrived at 5:05 p.m.)
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

City Council Minutes  1  January 5, 2009
 INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Kelley arrived at 5:05 p.m.

CLOSED SESSION

CS1.  Conference with Labor Negotiators: Agency designated representatives: City
  Manager Wilberg, Assistant City Manager Bornstein, City Attorney Curley,
  Deputy City Attorney Rusnak Unrepresented employees: All noncontract
  employees of the City of Mission Viejo regarding salaries; salary schedules and
  total compensation pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957.6.

CS2.  Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of
  Mission Viejo v. CUSD, Case No. 00180049; Companion Case, Rancho Santa
  Margarita v. CUSD, Case No. 00207543.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m. Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Closed Session item CS1, the Council received an
update on negotiations and those items are agendaized for action tonight under Consent Calendar
item 15. For item CS2, the parties continue to negotiate towards a settlement to try and eliminate
the need for prolonged litigation. The City is moving forward and further details will be
announced as the information becomes reportable.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Presentation to Former Mayor Kelley

  Mayor Ury presented Council Member Kelley with a gavel plaque in recognition of her
  service as Mayor in 2008.

P2.  Opening Remarks by Mayor Ury

  Mayor Ury discussed his goals for the year as he assumes the role of Mayor.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: commended volunteers who worked on the Rose Parade float but he
expressed opposition to the amount spent on the float. Mr. Gilbert referred to an article in

City Council Minutes  2  January 5, 2009
 today’s Orange County Register entitled "Editorial: Mission Viejo wins The Spendthrift City
Award for 2008."

Del Holt and Don Asay, M.V.: speaking on behalf of the Mission Viejo Activities Committee,
thanked city staff and the Council Members for all the cooperation and support that made the
relocation of Santa’s Workshop possible. Mr. Holt stated that there was overwhelming
acceptance and appreciation for the new, safer venue.

Helen Workun, M.V.: thanked the City Council for having the foresight and the courage to enter
a float in the 2009 Rose Parade. She stated that this was a spectacular way to showcase our City
and to celebrate its 20th anniversary; winning an award was just icing on the cake.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 7, 12, 13, 14 and 15 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve
the Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

3.  Summary of Fiscal Year 2008 - 2009 Budget Amendments to Date

  Received and filed.

4.  Check Register dated November 21, 2008, in the amount of $1,122,709.02

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated November 28, 2008, in the amount of $1,770,712.43

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Check Register dated December 5, 2008, in the amount of $811,293.86

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  3  January 5, 2009
 8.  Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report for October 2008

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for October 2008

  Received and filed.

10.  Mileage Reimbursement

  Approved the Resolution No. 09-01 Adopting the 2009 Standard IRS Mileage
  Reimbursement Rate of 55.0 Cents Per Mile Effective January 6, 2009.

11.  Renewal of Telecommunications Services with State of California and AT&T

  Approved contracts (A09-01) with the State of California to allow AT&T to provide local
  and long distance calling plans and other telecommunications services through December
  2010.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

16.  City Council Communication with Auditors

  Accounting Manager Bob Barry presented the staff report.

  Bob Calahan, Diehl, Evans & Company, LLP: outlined the audit process and stated that
  the CAFR document is presented fairly and complies with the State regulations for
  financial reporting. Mr. Calahan answered questions of the City Council Members.

  By consensus, the City Council received and filed correspondence from Diehl, Evans &
  Company, LLP, the City’s independent auditors, regarding the recently completed
  financial statement audit for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2008.

NEW BUSINESS

17.  Appointment of City Commission Members

  Council Member Kelley made the following nominations:

  Community Services Commission – Edwin Althof
  Investment Advisory Commission – Mervyn McCulloch
  Planning and Transportation Commission – Richard Atkinson

City Council Minutes  4  January 5, 2009
   Council Member Ledesma made the following nominations:

  Community Services Commission – Gloria Heer
  Investment Advisory Commission – Jay Standish
  Planning and Transportation Commission – Richard Schweinberg

  Mayor Ury made the following nominations:
  Community Services Commission – Tim Reid
  Senior member of the Community Services Commission – Les Sykes
  Investment Advisory Commission – Patrick Imburgia
  Planning and Transportation Commission – Peter Bastone

  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean made the following nominations:

  Community Services Commission – Ronald Ruef
  Senior member of the Community Services Commission – Helen Workun
  Planning and Transportation Commission – Richard Sandzimier

  Due to the low number of applications received, Mayor Pro Tem MacLean asked staff to
  seek additional applications and stated that he will make an appointment to the
  Investment Advisory Commission at a later date.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she was not prepared to make her nominations this
  evening.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed opposition to the appointment of Richard Atkinson
  and Peter Bastone to the Planning and Transportation Commission, and Patrick Imburgia
  to the Investment Advisory Commission.

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma,
  to appoint the nominated commissioners with the exception of Richard Atkinson, Peter
  Bastone, and Patrick Imburgia.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  appoint Rich Atkinson for the Planning and Transportation Commission.

City Council Minutes  5  January 5, 2009
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

  Motion was made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to appoint
  Peter Bastone to the Planning and Transportation Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

  Motion was made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley to appoint Patrick
  Imburgia to the Investment Advisory Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

18.  City Council Committee Representative Appointments

  Mayor Ury appointed representatives to committees/regional boards as follows:

  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency
  Representative - Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  Alternate - Mayor Ury

  Measure M Growth Management Area 9 and 10 Interjurisdictional Forum
  Representative - Council Member Ledesma
  Alternate - Council Member Kelley

  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency
  Representative - Council Member Ledesma
  Alternate - Council Member Kelley

  California Joint Powers Insurance Authority
  Representative - Council Member Schlicht
  Alternate – Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein

City Council Minutes  6  January 5, 2009
   Orange County Fire Authority Board of Directors
  Representative - Council Member Kelley
  Alternate - Council Member Ledesma

  Transportation Corridor System
  Representative - Mayor Ury
  Alternate - Council Member Schlicht

  League of California Cities and Orange County Division of the League of California
  Cities
  Representative - Mayor Ury
  Alternate - Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

  South Orange County Major Investment Study (SOCMIS) Policy Working Group
  Representative - Mayor Ury
  Alternate - Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG)
  Council Member Kelley

  Orange County Council of Governments General Assembly
  Representative - Council Member Schlicht
  Alternate - Council Member Ledesma

19.  City Ad Hoc Committee Review

  Mayor Ury disbanded all current ad hoc committees and stated that new committees will
  be reviewed and formed as necessary.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  approve the Minutes for (1) the regular City Council Meeting of December 1, 2008, as
  presented; and (2) the Adjourned Meeting/Strategic Planning Workshop of December 15,
  2008, as presented.

  AMENDED motion was made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council
  Member Ledesma, to amend the Minutes to reflect that the City Council ignored Council

City Council Minutes  7  January 5, 2009
   Member Schlicht’s request to include preservation of the Casta del Sol golf course in the
  five-year Strategic Plan.

  On roll call, said amended motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Ledesma, Schlicht
  NOES:  Kelley, MacLean, Ury
  ABSENT: None

  On roll call, said main motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

7.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for October 2008

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

12.  Purchase of One (1) Animal Services Vehicle to provide Animal Control Services for
  Aliso Viejo

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: asked why the City of Aliso Viejo does not purchase the vehicle
  directly.

  Motion was made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Kelley to
  award a purchase agreement for one (1) Animal Services Vehicle to Capistrano Ford in
  an amount not to exceed $62,960.01 (A09-02).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

City Council Minutes  8  January 5, 2009
 13.  Contract Award for the Design of the Cattery Expansion at the Mission Viejo
  Animal Services Center

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: expressed concern with the portion of the repair and replacement
  costs that Mission Viejo and Laguna Niguel will bear.

  Sharon Cody, M.V.: stated that she and the other individuals who volunteer at the shelter
  each week are insulted by the comments of the prior public speaker. Mrs. Cody outlined
  the need for the cattery expansion and the process for receipt and expenditure of funds.

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  (1) award the contract for the cattery expansion design at the Mission Viejo Animal
  Services Center to Rauhaus Freedenfeld & Associates (A09-03) in an amount not to
  exceed $37,290; and (2) adopt Resolution 09-02 Establishing a Capital Improvement
  Project and Budget Appropriation for the Cattery Expansion.

  AMENDED motion was made by Council Member Schlicht to set aside the prior motion
  and solicit a proposal from architect Todd Skenderian in Laguna Beach. Motion died for
  lack of a second.

  On roll call, said main motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

14.  Temporary Contract Planner Services for Community Development Department

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to
  approve Contract Amendment No. 3 with Hogle-Ireland Incorporated to increase the
  amount of the contract by $45,000, for a total of $170,000, and extend the term of the
  contract through May 31, 2009.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

City Council Minutes  9  January 5, 2009
 15.  Revisions to the City’s Salary Schedule

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented
  the staff report.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: expressed opposition to the proposed 2% salary increase for city
  employees.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  adopt Resolution 09-03 Revising the City’s Salary Schedule and Establishing Salary
  Ranges for Authorized Job Classifications.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR'S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

20.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Received the report from Council Member Kelley.

21.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Received the report from Council Member MacLean.

22.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Received the report from Council Member Ledesma.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Dennis Wilberg read a portion of an email he received today from a member of
staff who was grateful to have had the opportunity to be part of the Rose Parade Float project.
Despite the few remarks he has heard in opposition to the project, Mr. Wilberg noted that the
comments he received from volunteers during completion of the float and residents’ notes which
are posted on the City blog equate to the community’s tremendous support and gratitude for the
Rose Parade Float.

City Council Minutes  10  January 5, 2009
 City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Bill Curley wished everyone a happy New Year.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

23.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley echoed prior comments about the Rose Parade Float. She too received
many accolades from community members who were impressed and grateful for the opportunity
to see the City's float in the parade. Discussing the move of Santa’s Workshop, Council Member
Kelley thanked the Mission Viejo Activities Committee and city staff for helping to implement
the event at the new civic center location. She and her husband enjoyed the opportunity to
volunteer on two occasions and the response from members of the community was
overwhelming. She stated that this is one of the events that makes Mission Viejo so special.
Council Member Kelley announced that the Saddleback Valley Unified School District is
considering the closure of two Mission Viejo schools; La Tierra Elementary as well as O'Neill
Elementary. She has heard concerns from many individuals who are not in favor of the closures
and she therefore reminded residents that they can attend the SVUSD Board Meeting this
Thursday, January 8th, at which time the proposed school closures will be discussed. Council
Member Kelley reminded residents that the Community of Character Word for the Month of
January is perseverance and she stated that she is proud to announce the arrival of her first
grandchild, a boy named Dane who was born on December 27, 2008.

Council Member Ledesma

Wished residents of the community a happy New Year.

Council Member Schlicht

24.  Roundabout Study

  Motion was made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ledesma,
  to (1) delay presentation of the Roundabout Study until Council Member Schlicht is able
  to get a member appointed and seated on the Planning and Transportation Commission;
  and (2) direct staff to release the roundabout study for public viewing as soon as it is
  complete.

City Council Minutes  11  January 5, 2009
   On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Ledesma, Schlicht
  NOES:  Kelley, MacLean, Ury
  ABSENT: None

25.  Creation of By-laws for Ad Hoc Committees

  Mayor Ury ruled that this item was out of order.

  Motion was made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ledesma,
  to over-rule the decision of the Mayor.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Ledesma, Schlicht
  NOES:  Kelley, MacLean, Ury
  ABSENT: None

Council Member Schlicht expressed dissatisfaction with the fact that she was not allowed to
place items under her own name on the December 1, 2008, Agenda. She respectfully requested
that she be treated with consistency and fairness as she serves on the City Council. Council
Member Schlicht announced that Angel Food Ministries helps those in need obtain food for half-
price. There are no restrictions, conditions or forms to be completed and she will leave the
information flier with the City Clerk for those who are interested in finding out more. She stated
that everybody seems to ignore the fact that the City paid for the Rose Parade float with tax
payer dollars but with two cities named Mission Viejo in the United States, Council Member
Schlicht wondered who really benefited from the float. She concluded her comments by wishing
everyone a very happy New Year.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean expressed his strong support for the Rose Parade Float. He thanked
the volunteers who contributed thousands of hours and city staff who coordinated the many
details. He stated that the project was great for building community and we have received an
overwhelming number of accolades and support, in addition to a Judge’s award. Mayor Pro Tem
MacLean discussed the move of Santa’s house and stated that it turned out to be a very positive
change. Although it was the first year in the new location, there were an increased number of
attendees. He asked the City Manager to publicize, on the City’s electronic message board, the
SVUSD’s public meeting regarding proposed school closures. The meeting will be held on

City Council Minutes  12  January 5, 2009
 Thursday, January 8, 2009 at 6:15 p.m. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean requested that Mayor Ury
close the meeting in honor of William Rudell, attorney with Richards Watson and Gershon.

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury congratulated Council Member Kelley and her family on the new baby. He also
congratulated the new commissioners and stated that he looks forward to the service they will be
providing to the City. He asked the City Clerk to give each Council Member a reusable memory
stick for storing the electronic version of the Agenda packets. The memory sticks will need to be
returned after each meeting for re-use and they will eliminate the need for multiple DVD’s by
providing a meeting archive in one location. Mayor Ury wished everyone a happy New Year
and he stated that he believes 2009 will be a great year for the city and a wonderful year for the
citizens of Mission Viejo.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:25 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in memory of William Rudell to Monday, January 19,
2009, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of January 19, 2009

City Council Minutes  13  January 5, 2009
